interfaces.name: Leave-one-column-out submatrix
interfaces.type_shape: Two arbitrary real matrices differing by their last column; no mixture model or randomness is assumed.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Two arbitrary real matrices differing by their last column; no mixture model or randomness is assumed.

members.statement_original:
Consider two matrices
\[
Y=(y_1,\ldots,y_{n-1})\in\mathbb R^{p\times(n-1)}\text{ and }\hat Y=(y_1,\ldots,y_{n-1},y_n)\in\mathbb R^{p\times n},
\]
(1)
where $Y$ is a leave-one-column-out submatrix of $\hat Y$ with the last column removed.

interfaces.name: Singular Value Decomposition
interfaces.type_shape: Ordered singular decompositions and their leading left-vector matrices in the arbitrary-matrix setup; sigma_{r+1} at the last allowed index has no explicit zero-extension convention in this passage.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Ordered singular decompositions and their leading left-vector matrices in the arbitrary-matrix setup; sigma_{r+1} at the last allowed index has no explicit zero-extension convention in this passage.

members.statement_original:
Consider two matrices as in (1) such that they are equal to each other except that $\hat Y$ has an extra last column. Let the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of these two matrices be
\[
Y=\sum_{i\in[p\wedge(n-1)]}\sigma_i u_iv_i^T\text{ and }\hat Y=\sum_{i\in[p\wedge n]}\hat\sigma_i\hat u_i\hat v_i^T,
\]
where $\sigma_1\geq\ldots\geq\sigma_{p\wedge(n-1)}$ and $\hat\sigma_1\geq\ldots\geq\hat\sigma_{p\wedge n}$. Consider any $r\in[p\wedge(n-1)]$. Define
\[
U_r:=(u_1,\ldots,u_r)\in\mathbb O^{p\times r}\text{ and }\hat U_r:=(\hat u_1,\ldots,\hat u_r)\in\mathbb O^{p\times r}
\]
to include the leading $r$ left singular vectors of $Y$ and $\hat Y$, respectively.

interfaces.name: Mixture model
interfaces.type_shape: Fixed centers and assignments with arbitrary noise vectors. Independence and distributions are additional theorem hypotheses, not part of the general mixture model.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Fixed centers and assignments with arbitrary noise vectors. Independence and distributions are additional theorem hypotheses, not part of the general mixture model.

members.statement_original:
We consider a mixture model with $k$ centers $\theta_1^*,\theta_2^*,\ldots,\theta_k^*\in\mathbb R^p$ and a cluster assignment vector $z^*\in[k]^n$. The observations $X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n\in\mathbb R^p$ are generated from
\[
X_i=\theta_{z_i^*}^*+\epsilon_i,
\]
(6)
where $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n\in\mathbb R^p$ are noises.

interfaces.name: Data matrix
interfaces.type_shape: Original matrix representation of the mixture observations, including the named signal and noise matrices. No probabilistic restriction is added.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original matrix representation of the mixture observations, including the named signal and noise matrices. No probabilistic restriction is added.

members.statement_original:
The data matrix $X:=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$ can be written equivalently in a matrix form
\[
X=P+E,
\]
(7)
where $P:=(\theta_{z_1^*}^*,\theta_{z_2^*}^*,\ldots,\theta_{z_n^*}^*)$ is the signal matrix and $E:=(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n)$ is the noise matrix.

interfaces.name: Smallest cluster size
interfaces.type_shape: Normalized minimum cluster size. The different powers of k and numerical bounds in each theorem remain distinct local hypotheses.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Normalized minimum cluster size. The different powers of k and numerical bounds in each theorem remain distinct local hypotheses.

members.statement_original: Define $\beta:=\frac1{n/k}\min_{a\in[k]}|\{i:z_i^*=a\}|$ such that $\beta n/k$ is the smallest cluster size.

interfaces.name: Leave-one-out counterparts
interfaces.type_shape: Remove each specified column from the mixture data matrix; not a change to the true assignments or noise law.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Remove each specified column from the mixture data matrix; not a change to the true assignments or noise law.

members.statement_original:
We are interested in the left singular subspaces of $X$ and its leave-one-out counterparts. For each $i\in[n]$, define $X_{-i}$ to be a submatrix of $X$ with its $i$th column removed. That is,
\[
X_{-i}:=(X_1,\ldots,X_{i-1},X_{i+1},\ldots,X_n)\in\mathbb R^{p\times(n-1)}.
\]
(8)

interfaces.name: Left singular vectors
interfaces.type_shape: Empirical full-data and leave-one-out singular-vector matrices. These are not the signal-matrix singular vectors. The k-based index domain is retained without silently extending a finite SVD.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Empirical full-data and leave-one-out singular-vector matrices. These are not the signal-matrix singular vectors. The k-based index domain is retained without silently extending a finite SVD.

members.statement_original:
Let their SVDs be $X=\sum_{j\in[p\wedge n]}\hat\lambda_j\hat u_j\hat v_j^T$ and $X_{-i}=\sum_{j\in[p\wedge(n-1)]}\hat\lambda_{-i,j}\hat u_{-i,j}\hat v_{-i,j}^T$, where $\hat\lambda_1\geq\hat\lambda_2\geq\ldots\geq\hat\lambda_{p\wedge n}$ and $\hat\lambda_{-i,1}\geq\hat\lambda_{-i,2}\geq\ldots\geq\hat\lambda_{-i,p\wedge(n-1)}$. Note that the signal matrix $P$ is at most rank-$k$. Then for any $r\in[k]$, define
\[
\hat U_{1:r}:=(\hat u_1,\hat u_2,\ldots,\hat u_r)\in\mathbb O^{p\times r}\text{ and }\hat U_{-i,1:r}=(\hat u_{-i,1},\ldots,\hat u_{-i,r})\in\mathbb O^{p\times r}
\]
to include the leading $r$ left singular vectors of $X$ and $X_{-i}$, respectively.

interfaces.name: Singular values
interfaces.type_shape: Population signal singular values and positive rank kappa, distinct from empirical hatted singular values. Kappa may be smaller than k.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Population signal singular values and positive rank kappa, distinct from empirical hatted singular values. Kappa may be smaller than k.

members.statement_original: Let $\lambda_1\geq\lambda_2\geq\ldots\geq\lambda_{p\wedge n}$ be the singular values of $P$ and $\kappa$ be the rank of $P$ such that $\kappa\in[k]$, $\lambda_\kappa>0$, and $\lambda_{\kappa+1}=0$.

interfaces.name: Spectral Clustering
interfaces.type_shape: Full two-step source algorithm with an exact global k-means minimizer. Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 choose r=kappa and r=k respectively. Approximate k-means in Discussion is not substituted.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Full two-step source algorithm with an exact global k-means minimizer. Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 choose r=kappa and r=k respectively. Approximate k-means in Discussion is not substituted.

members.statement_original:
Algorithm 1: Spectral Clustering

Input: Data matrix $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$, number of clusters $k$, number of singular vectors $r$

Output: Cluster assignment vector $\hat z\in[k]^n$

1 Perform SVD on $X$ to have
\[
X=\sum_{i=1}^{p\wedge n}\hat\lambda_i\hat u_i\hat v_i^T,
\]
where $\hat\lambda_1\geq\hat\lambda_2\geq\ldots\geq\hat\lambda_{p\wedge n}\geq0$ and $\{\hat u_i\}_{i=1}^{p\wedge n}\in\mathbb R^p,\{\hat v_i\}_{i=1}^{p\wedge n}\in\mathbb R^n$. Let $\hat U_{1:r}:=(\hat u_1,\ldots,\hat u_r)\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}$.

2 Perform $k$-means on the columns of $\hat U_{1:r}^TX$. That is,
\[
\left(\hat z,\{\hat c_j\}_{j\in[k]}\right)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in[k]^n,\{c_j\}_{j\in[k]}\in\mathbb R^r}\sum_{i\in[n]}\|\hat U_{1:r}^TX_i-c_{z_i}\|^2.
\]
(14)

interfaces.name: Misclustering error
interfaces.type_shape: Preserve the printed equality inside the indicator. Equation (17) on the same page instead counts inequalities; this source discrepancy is separately flagged, not silently corrected.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Preserve the printed equality inside the indicator. Equation (17) on the same page instead counts inequalities; this source discrepancy is separately flagged, not silently corrected.

members.statement_original:
For any $z\in[k]^n$, its misclustering error is defined as
\[
\ell(z,z^*):=\min_{\phi\in\Phi}\frac1n\sum_{i\in[n]}\mathbb I\{z_i=\phi(z_i^*)\},
\]
where $\Phi:=\{\phi:\phi\text{ is a bijection from }[k]\text{ to }[k]\}$. The minimization of $\Phi$ is due to that the cluster assignment vector $z^*$ is identifiable only up to a permutation of the labels $[k]$.

interfaces.name: Minimum distance among centers
interfaces.type_shape: Minimum Euclidean distance between distinct cluster centers. The real-delta parameterization of the two-cluster model is retained separately with its sign issue.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Minimum Euclidean distance between distinct cluster centers. The real-delta parameterization of the two-cluster model is retained separately with its sign issue.

members.statement_original:
Define $\Delta$ to be the minimum distance among centers, i.e.,
\[
\Delta:=\min_{a,b\in[k]:a\ne b}\|\theta_a^*-\theta_b^*\|.
\]

interfaces.name: Sub-Gaussian
interfaces.type_shape: Scalar uncentered moment-generating-function bound for every real t; no subtraction of the mean is inserted. The variance proxy sigma squared is distinct from actual variance bar-sigma squared.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Scalar uncentered moment-generating-function bound for every real t; no subtraction of the mean is inserted. The variance proxy sigma squared is distinct from actual variance bar-sigma squared.

members.statement_original: For a random variable $X$, we say $X$ is sub-Gaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2$ (denoted as $X\sim\mathrm{SG}(\sigma^2)$) if $\mathbb Ee^{tX}\leq\exp(\sigma^2t^2/2)$ for any $t\in\mathbb R$.

interfaces.name: Sub-Gaussian random vector
interfaces.type_shape: Common scalar variance proxy in every unit direction, not coordinatewise independence. Theorem-specific independence across observations remains separate.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Common scalar variance proxy in every unit direction, not coordinatewise independence. Theorem-specific independence across observations remains separate.

members.statement_original: For a random vector $X\in\mathbb R^d$, we say $X$ is sub-Gaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2$ (denoted as $X\sim\mathrm{SG}_d(\sigma^2)$) if $u^TX\sim\mathrm{SG}(\sigma^2)$ for any unit vector $u\in\mathbb R^d$.

naming_context.text: Theorem 3.1 assumes that each noise $\epsilon_i$ is an independent sub-Gaussian random vector with zero mean and variance proxy $\sigma^2$ and establishes an exponential rate for the risk $\mathbb E\ell(\hat z,z^*)$.

interfaces.name: Spectral Clustering with Adaptive Dimension Reduction
interfaces.type_shape: Full adaptive algorithm. Import only Step 1 of Algorithm 1 as auxiliary A3; not its fixed-r clustering output. Preserve largest-index choice and the printed non-strict gap threshold. No empty-set fallback is supplied in the source.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Full adaptive algorithm. Import only Step 1 of Algorithm 1 as auxiliary A3; not its fixed-r clustering output. Preserve largest-index choice and the printed non-strict gap threshold. No empty-set fallback is supplied in the source.

members.source_heading: Algorithm 2 — Spectral Clustering with Adaptive Dimension Reduction
members.statement_original:
Algorithm 2: Spectral Clustering with Adaptive Dimension Reduction

Input: Data matrix $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$, number of clusters $k$, threshold $T$

Output: Clustering label vector $\tilde z\in[k]^n$

1 Perform SVD on $X$ same as Step 1 of Algorithm 1.

2 Let $\hat r$ be the largest index in $[k]$ such that the difference between two neighboring singular values is greater than $T$, i.e.,
\[
\hat r=\max\{a\in[k]:\hat\lambda_a-\hat\lambda_{a+1}\geq T\}.
\]
(23)
Let $\hat U_{1:\hat r}:=(\hat u_1,\ldots,\hat u_{\hat r})\in\mathbb R^{p\times\hat r}$.

3 Perform $k$-means on the columns of $\hat U_{1:\hat r}^TX$. That is,
\[
\left(\tilde z,\{\tilde c_j\}_{j=1}^k\right)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in[k]^n,\{c_j\}_{j=1}^k\in\mathbb R^{\hat r}}\sum_{i\in[n]}\|\hat U_{1:\hat r}^TX_i-c_{z_i}\|^2.
\]
(24)

interfaces.name: Two-cluster symmetric mixture model
interfaces.type_shape: Two opposite constant-coordinate centers and iid noise entries across both samples and coordinates. The statement allows real delta; no positive sign is inserted.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Two opposite constant-coordinate centers and iid noise entries across both samples and coordinates. The statement allows real delta; no positive sign is inserted.

members.statement_original:
Consider a mixture model (6) with two clusters such that
\[
\theta_1^*=-\theta_2^*=\delta\mathbf1_p,\text{ and }\{\epsilon_{i,j}\}_{i\in[n],j\in[p]}\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim F,
\]
(28)
for some $\delta\in\mathbb R$ and some distribution $F$, where $\{\epsilon_{i,j}\}_{j\in[p]}$ are entries of $\epsilon_i$ for each $i\in[n]$.

naming_context.text: To answer this question, in this section we consider a two-cluster symmetric mixture model where the centers are proportional to $\mathbf1_p$ and the noises have i.i.d. entries.

interfaces.name: Spectral estimator
interfaces.type_shape: Two-means applied to the empirical leading singular-vector projection. It is not a sign estimator, and the true singular vector is not substituted for the empirical one. A3 retains the SVD convention used here.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Two-means applied to the empirical leading singular-vector projection. It is not a sign estimator, and the true singular vector is not substituted for the empirical one. A3 retains the SVD convention used here.

members.statement_original:
Define
\[
\left(\check z,\{\check c_j\}_{j=1}^2\right)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in[2]^n,\{c_j\}_{j=1}^2\in\mathbb R}\sum_{i\in[n]}(\hat u_1^TX_i-c_{z_i})^2.
\]
(29)
The performance of the spectral estimator $\check z$ will be the focus in this section.

interfaces.name: Fisher information
interfaces.type_shape: Original regularity assumptions and Fisher-information definition from Lemma 3.4, explicitly imported by Theorem 3.5. Delta is fixed in that lemma; it is not replaced by a growing-separation limit.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original regularity assumptions and Fisher-information definition from Lemma 3.4, explicitly imported by Theorem 3.5. Delta is fixed in that lemma; it is not replaced by a growing-separation limit.

members.statement_original: Assume the distribution $F$ has a positive, continuously differentiable density $f$ with mean zero and finite Fisher information $\mathcal I:=\int(f'/f)^2f\,dx$. Assume $\Delta$ is a constant.
